A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, A Layer-wise Analysis of Supervised Fine-Tuning. The text, equations, Figures 1–7, Tables 1–4, and Appendices A–C are available and can be reliably matched despite reference additions and appendix reflow.

before.justification: Sections 4.2–4.4 report original representation measurements, probing, layer-swapping, and selective-LoRA experiments. Appendices A–B report segment-sensitivity accuracies and knowledge-retention perplexities.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical outcomes, including the main experimental figures and the sensitivity and perplexity results in Appendices A–B.

M1.justification: The layer-wise analytical framework and Mid-Block Efficient Tuning procedure are unchanged. Section 4.4 retains the same selective allocation of LoRA parameters across layer segments.

E1.justification: Both versions use MMLU, GSM8K, WikiText, IFEval, HumanEval, MT-Bench, and ToxiGen with the same task coverage. Question generation is added only as a related-work example in Section 2.1.

E2.justification: The Base/SFT comparisons, full-layer LoRA baseline, and segment-specific configurations remain unchanged in the corresponding experiments. The four added references introduce no evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Sections 3.5 and 4.1–4.4 retain the same metrics, checkpoints, reported 100-instance token-level and 1,000-instance pooled analyses, and LoRA settings. Appendix A retains the same three- and ten-segment evaluation protocols.

E4.justification: The probing, weight-change correlations, layer-swapping analysis, segment-boundary sensitivity tests, and knowledge-retention analysis are all retained. Appendix table relocation introduces no new ablation or robustness evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same fixed-seed disclosure in Section 4.1 and different-seed robustness check with a t-test reporting p < 0.01 in Section 4.2. No run-count or uncertainty-reporting changes are introduced.

E6.justification: Figures 1–7 and the appendix results are unchanged. For example, Tables 1–2 retain peak accuracies of 0.4721 and 0.4771, while Table 4 retains middle-segment perplexities of 14.54 and 13.60 versus full-layer LoRA's 14.70 and 13.76.

T1.justification: Section 3 retains the same mathematical definitions and Equations 1–10, including weight-change, entropy, effective-rank, curvature, and alignment metrics. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of depth-dependent adaptation, stable intermediate layers, sensitive final layers, and benefits from Mid-Block Efficient Tuning. The added citations do not alter the contribution's scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning late-layer plasticity, intermediate-layer knowledge integration, and catastrophic forgetting are unchanged. The limitations concerning dense decoder-only architectures, SFT-only analysis, and empirical block boundaries are also retained.

D1.justification: The checkpoint identifiers, streaming representation computation, sparsity threshold, LoRA settings, and code-access links are unchanged. v2 provides no additional implementation or reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v2 adds four Zhao et al. references: two question-generation works and two knowledge-graph alignment works. The introduction adds the latter citations, and Section 2.1 adds question generation as an SFT application. The paper's novelty positioning otherwise remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Textual edits are limited to citation insertions, the brief question-generation addition in Section 2.1, and corresponding bibliography entries. The scientific sections and appendix narrative retain their wording and organization.

P2.justification: The expanded bibliography shifts appendix layout: Table 2 moves from page 11 to page 12, and Tables 3–4 move from page 12 to a separate page 13. Table content and formatting are retained; Figures 1–7 are visually unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 adds limited literature context through four references and a question-generation example, while retaining the same methods, evidence, claims, reproducibility information, and limitations. Appendix reflow separates Tables 3–4 from their discussion without changing their content. These contextual and layout edits produce no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
